title: Build a Complete CSS Website
subtitle: A short practical refresher followed by 20 new application questions
description: Review the ten CSS dashboard topics. Includes three capstone examples and exactly two fresh review questions from each of Lessons 1–10.

blocks.text: Welcome to the CSS final review. This lesson is intentionally shorter on new theory and longer on practical decisions. You will revisit the ten dashboard topics and answer two new application questions for each lesson, for exactly 20 questions.

Start by reading the requirement, tracing where its data comes from, and deciding what success should look like. Then test both a normal case and a boundary or failure case. A correct program should not only work once; it should behave predictably when its inputs change.

Practice direction: Open Home → Menu → Practical/Practice → select CSS. Paste this snippet into the matching web/React editor, run or preview it, and compare what happens. Then change one value or element and run it again so you can observe the effect. If this course is not available in the in-app runner, use a suitable compiler or interpreter for the language.

blocks.text: Use the third example as a starting point, then explain how it relates to the course topic: Put selectors, layout, typography, responsiveness, effects and visual design together in a complete project.

Answer two questions from each dashboard lesson. These questions are newly written for this review and are not copied from the corresponding lesson quizzes. Read carefully: select the option that best satisfies the requirement, not merely an option that could work in a different situation.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 1 — Introduction to CSS: A team receives a repository with no run instructions. What should the maintainer add to make a fresh setup verifiable?
options: A setup/run guide plus a minimal test or sample command.
Only a screenshot of the editor.
A statement that setup is obvious.
blocks.explanation: A reproducible setup guide helps another developer validate the project from a clean start.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A reproducible setup guide helps another developer validate the project from a clean start.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A reproducible setup guide helps another developer validate the project from a clean start.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 1 — Introduction to CSS: The app works after manual edits but fails when built from source. What should be compared?
options: The actual source, compiler/runtime configuration, and documented build path.
blocks.explanation: Build and runtime configuration are part of a reproducible program, not separate from it.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Build and runtime configuration are part of a reproducible program, not separate from it.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Build and runtime configuration are part of a reproducible program, not separate from it.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 2 — CSS Selectors: A component class is reused across many cards, but an ID is also reused across all cards. What should be corrected?
options: Use a class for reusable styling and keep IDs unique.
Replace the class with inline styles on every property.
blocks.explanation: Classes are reusable; IDs should identify a unique element.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Classes are reusable; IDs should identify a unique element.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Classes are reusable; IDs should identify a unique element.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 2 — CSS Selectors: A CSS declaration is crossed out in developer tools. What is the best investigation?
options: Inspect specificity, cascade order, and the winning rule.
blocks.explanation: The cascade decides which declaration wins; inspect the competing rules before editing.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. The cascade decides which declaration wins; inspect the competing rules before editing.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. The cascade decides which declaration wins; inspect the competing rules before editing.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 3 — Colors, Backgrounds and Borders: A white label overlays a bright image and becomes unreadable in parts. What is the most effective fix?
options: Ensure sufficient contrast with a stable overlay/background or alternate placement.
blocks.explanation: Readable contrast should hold across the real background, not only in one image region.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Readable contrast should hold across the real background, not only in one image region.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Readable contrast should hold across the real background, not only in one image region.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 3 — Colors, Backgrounds and Borders: The same spacing and color values appear throughout the site. What helps keep the design consistent?
options: Randomly choose new values each page.
Use image screenshots instead of CSS.
blocks.explanation: Shared variables allow consistent, controlled design updates.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Shared variables allow consistent, controlled design updates.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Shared variables allow consistent, controlled design updates.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 4 — CSS Box Model: A card’s outer width is unexpectedly larger than its declared width after padding is added. What rule may simplify sizing?
options: float: none on an unrelated element
blocks.explanation: Border-box includes padding and borders within the declared width.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Border-box includes padding and borders within the declared width.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Border-box includes padding and borders within the declared width.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 4 — CSS Box Model: Content is too close to a card edge, but the card is correctly positioned relative to neighbors. Which property is likely needed?
blocks.explanation: Padding changes internal spacing without moving the card relative to surrounding elements.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Padding changes internal spacing without moving the card relative to surrounding elements.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Padding changes internal spacing without moving the card relative to surrounding elements.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 5 — Typography and Text Styling: A page is readable on desktop but body text clips at 200% zoom. What should be addressed?
options: Add fixed heights to every paragraph.
Allow text and containers to resize/wrap and retest.
Use a smaller font at all sizes.
blocks.explanation: Layout must tolerate zoom and variable text size without clipping content.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Layout must tolerate zoom and variable text size without clipping content.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Layout must tolerate zoom and variable text size without clipping content.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 5 — Typography and Text Styling: The title hierarchy is unclear even though the colors differ. What should be tuned?
options: Semantic headings plus a consistent scale of size, weight, and spacing.
blocks.explanation: Structure and deliberate typography work together to establish hierarchy.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Structure and deliberate typography work together to establish hierarchy.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Structure and deliberate typography work together to establish hierarchy.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 6 — CSS Flexbox: A toolbar must keep the logo at one end and actions at the other while vertically aligning them. Which property pair is relevant?
options: justify-content and align-items in a flex container.
blocks.explanation: Flexbox alignment properties distribute along the main and cross axes.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Flexbox alignment properties distribute along the main and cross axes.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Flexbox alignment properties distribute along the main and cross axes.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 6 — CSS Flexbox: Cards should flow onto a new row on narrow screens. What property should be reviewed?
blocks.explanation: Flex wrapping allows items to move onto additional lines when space is limited.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Flex wrapping allows items to move onto additional lines when space is limited.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Flex wrapping allows items to move onto additional lines when space is limited.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 7 — CSS Grid: A dashboard has both aligned columns and rows. What is a direct Grid feature for defining the column tracks?
blocks.explanation: grid-template-columns defines the grid’s column tracks.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. grid-template-columns defines the grid’s column tracks.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. grid-template-columns defines the grid’s column tracks.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 7 — CSS Grid: A card grid must remain responsive when the available width changes. Which approach is best?
options: Use absolute positioning for all cards.
Use flexible tracks and a sensible minmax minimum.
blocks.explanation: Flexible tracks let the grid adapt while preventing cards from shrinking too far.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Flexible tracks let the grid adapt while preventing cards from shrinking too far.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Flexible tracks let the grid adapt while preventing cards from shrinking too far.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 8 — Responsive Web Design: A layout breaks between two tested widths. What should guide the breakpoint?
options: The point where the actual content needs a different arrangement.
The brand name of a phone.
The total number of CSS rules.
The date the page was published.
blocks.explanation: Content-driven breakpoints respond to layout needs rather than device labels.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Content-driven breakpoints respond to layout needs rather than device labels.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Content-driven breakpoints respond to layout needs rather than device labels.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 8 — Responsive Web Design: A large image forces a phone page wider than the viewport. What simple CSS rule often prevents that?
blocks.explanation: Responsive image sizing prevents overflow while retaining aspect ratio.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Responsive image sizing prevents overflow while retaining aspect ratio.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Responsive image sizing prevents overflow while retaining aspect ratio.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 9 — Animations and Transitions: An animation provides no information and distracts from reading. What should the designer do?
options: Remove or reduce it and honor reduced-motion preferences.
Move the text while the user reads it.
blocks.explanation: Motion should support the task and accommodate reduced-motion preferences.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Motion should support the task and accommodate reduced-motion preferences.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Motion should support the task and accommodate reduced-motion preferences.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 9 — Animations and Transitions: A hover effect should not cause nearby content to jump. What technique is generally preferable for visual movement?
options: Change the element’s margin drastically every frame.
Use transform for movement when appropriate.
blocks.explanation: Transforms are suited to visual movement without changing normal document flow.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Transforms are suited to visual movement without changing normal document flow.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Transforms are suited to visual movement without changing normal document flow.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 10 — Build a Complete CSS Website: The final project passes one example input. What is the strongest completion check?
options: Stop testing as soon as the screen appears.
Remove error handling to reduce lines.
Test normal, boundary, empty, and failure cases and document how to run it.
blocks.explanation: Broader tests and reproducible setup provide stronger evidence than one happy-path example.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Broader tests and reproducible setup provide stronger evidence than one happy-path example.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Broader tests and reproducible setup provide stronger evidence than one happy-path example.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 10 — Build a Complete CSS Website: A teammate cannot reproduce the project’s behavior. What is likely missing?
options: Repeatable instructions, clear dependencies, and a testable expected result.
blocks.explanation: Reproducibility requires enough source and setup information for another person to verify the same behavior.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Reproducibility requires enough source and setup information for another person to verify the same behavior.
